findings.where: Explain, paragraph 3, and screen 11's Why? note
findings.what: "Textbooks add that this is one reason air compressors are cooled" has no citation: the lesson's sources list holds no compressor source, and the research has only one SECONDARY lecture note (notes 4.12), which says isothermal compression "consumed the minimum work" and says nothing about why compressors are cooled. Calling that one note "Textbooks" makes it sound like more than it is, so cite it as a lecture note or drop the sentence.

findings.where: Screen 11 (Which takes less work?), its Why? note, and explain paragraph 3
findings.what: "The steady-temperature squeeze takes less work" is true only for the same end volume of 0.1 m³, and that is not how a compressor is compared. Squeezed from 200 kPa at 0.2 m³ to the same end pressure of 400 kPa, the n = 1.3 gas stops at about 0.117 m³ and takes about 23.13 kJ against 27.73 kJ. So say "to the same end volume", and do not tie this comparison to compressor cooling: a compressor saves work over its delivery cycle at a set pressure ratio, and this lesson does not show that.

findings.where: Explain, paragraph 3 ("squeezing it from 0.2 to 0.1 m³ takes 30.82 kJ")
findings.what: "It" reads as the n = 1.3 gas that has just expanded to 0.2 m³. That gas is at 162 kPa and would take only 25.03 kJ to squeeze back. The 30.82 kJ figure needs the squeeze to start at 200 kPa, as screen 11's task says, so the explain text must say so.

findings.where: Analogy (E12 series) and practice (1 bar = 100 kPa)
findings.what: The E12 values (twelve in every × 10: 10, 12, 15, and so on up to 82, then 100) and 1 bar = 100 kPa are listed as constants with no source, which breaks the rule that every number is a control, computed or a cited constant. Cite IEC 60063 or a maker's table, and a units reference for the bar, or label them as unsourced.

findings.where: Screens 8 and 10, the Double it button with Squeeze it on
findings.what: With Squeeze it on, Double it sets the larger volume to twice the smaller, so V₂ ends at half of V₁, not "twice V₁" as screen 4 and the description say. Relabel the button "Halve it" while squeezing, or word it as "the start volume twice the end".

findings.where: Screen 6 (The stretch that adds C), second readout and say line
findings.what: The readout labelled C × ln(V₂ ÷ V₁), and the line "where the area under the curve is 39.95 kJ", show the overshoot shrinking by using the ln rule before the screen has earned it. Measuring the area up to the last bar's end with 100 mid-height bars, as screens 1-5 did, would stop the argument from resting on its own conclusion.

The step from "the area from V₁ to e × V₁ is exactly C" to W = C × ln(V₂ ÷ V₁) appears only as a small form note. That step is: each further stretch by e adds another C, so the work is C times the number of e-stretches, and that number is ln of the ratio, lesson 4's "power you need". Say it in the screen's own words, and untangle the last sentence ("with one part it is 40 × ln 2, ln 2 being about 0.693, the hundred bars' total from 0.1 to 0.2 m³").

findings.where: Screen 14, the key inside the drawing ("shaded: ln 3 ≈ 1.099")
findings.what: In the drawing's sans face, ln reads as "In". The lesson already sets ln in its typewriter face (.lnk) in the text so the l is never taken for a capital I, but the SVG key does not use it.

x is italic in "y = 1 ÷ x" but upright in "shaded from 1 to x", "ln x" and "Drag x along", and C in "C = 1" is upright. The screen also says "so the shaded area is ln x" without the one-line reason: C × ln(x ÷ 1), with C = 1 and V₁ = 1.

findings.where: Screen 14 text ("ln x climbs by about 1 ÷ x for each 1 along")
findings.what: This reads as a climb over the next whole unit: from 1 to 2, ln x climbs 0.693, not 1. Say "climbs at a rate of 1 ÷ x", or "by about h ÷ x for each small step h".

The Bars control already shows 4 selected while no bars are drawn for the first 2.2 s. The hidden readouts and waiting form lines also leave a tall blank band above Play again. The opening picture would look more alive if the 4 bars stood from the start, or if the control appeared with them.
